title: A Comprehensive Exploration of Personalized Learning in Smart Education: From Student Modeling to Personalized Recommendations
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the broad question of how personalized learning in smart education has been defined, theorized, implemented, and studied in recent years, with particular emphasis on AI-enabled student modeling and personalized recommendation. The authors argue that prior reviews have often focused on isolated components, such as learning styles or recommendation algorithms, and therefore lack a unified account of the field. To address this gap, they conduct a comprehensive survey of literature published roughly between 2017 and 2025, covering definitions, goals, educational theories, technical methods, applications, challenges, and future directions.

The review centers on two core technical components of personalized learning: student modeling and personalized recommendations. Student modeling is divided into cognitive and non-cognitive dimensions, including cognitive diagnosis, student performance prediction, learning style analysis, sentiment analysis, and behavior analysis. Personalized recommendation is organized into learning path, course, and exercise recommendation. The paper also links these computational approaches to educational theories such as progressivism, behaviorism, constructivism, cognitive psychology, and sociocultural theory, arguing that these theories provide the pedagogical basis for AI-driven personalization.

The paper is not a primary intervention study with a single participant sample; instead, it reviews approximately 486 retained articles, supplemented through backward snowballing, from major conferences and journals. As a result, no single learner population or implementation setting is the focus, although the discussion spans multiple educational contexts including traditional classrooms, online education, workforce training, and career development. The review consistently discusses students as the primary target of personalized learning systems and educators as key users of diagnostic and recommendation outputs.

The main conclusion is that personalized learning has become a mature and rapidly expanding area in intelligent education, with strong promise for improving engagement, adapting instruction to learner differences, supporting academic performance, and enabling more flexible learning pathways. At the same time, the authors conclude that major challenges remain, especially around data quality, assessment systems, technological limitations, interpretability, and ethics. They advocate for future work that better integrates educational theory with data-driven AI methods and that strengthens real-world applicability, fairness, and trustworthiness in personalized learning systems.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: Intelligent educational systems for personalized learning that combine student modeling and personalized recommendation/adaptation, including cognitive diagnosis, learning path/course/exercise recommendation, and adaptive instructional support.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper is a comprehensive survey/review of personalized learning in smart education, synthesizing research on intelligent educational systems broadly rather than evaluating one specific product. It reviews student modeling and personalized recommendation methods, and references application cases such as adaptive quizzing, gamified learning platforms, and intelligent tutoring systems as examples.

findings.finding_summary: The review states that personalized learning enhances engagement, improves learning outcomes, and accommodates diverse educational needs, and that it has demonstrated effectiveness across traditional classrooms, online education, workforce training, and career development. However, no pooled effect sizes, confidence intervals, or aggregate sample sizes are reported in the provided text.
findings.measure: General learning outcomes and engagement across reviewed personalized learning applications

findings.finding_summary: In the cognitive diagnosis section, the review cites an empirical study applying a DINA-based cognitive diagnosis in a high-school physics course on electromagnetic induction, reporting significantly greater learning gains in the experimental group than in the control group when multi-level remedial instruction was designed from diagnostic results. The excerpt does not report effect size, confidence interval, or sample size.
findings.measure: Learning gains in high-school physics (electromagnetic induction) following DINA-based diagnostic-informed remedial instruction

identified_tools.name: Khan Academy
identified_tools.description: An online learning platform that includes adaptive quizzing and instructional support features.
identified_tools.use_case: Mentioned as an example application of behaviorist theory in personalized learning through adaptive quizzing systems; not directly evaluated in this review.

identified_tools.name: Duolingo
identified_tools.description: A gamified language-learning platform that personalizes practice and feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: Mentioned as an example gamified learning platform illustrating behaviorist theory in personalized learning; not directly evaluated in this review.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a review/survey article synthesizing prior literature on personalized learning systems, but the provided text does not report a formal meta-analysis with pooled quantitative estimates or a clearly specified evidence-synthesis protocol tied to outcomes. As presented, it is best treated as review-level synthesis with limited extractable causal evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The review describes generally positive effects of personalized learning, but the excerpt does not provide pooled effect sizes or consistent quantitative outcome magnitudes. Impact is therefore positive but unclear in size.
